name: Azmaveth
overview: Azmaveth was a male figure known as the Barhumite, identified as the twenty-first member among "the thirty," a group of David's mighty men. His tribal affiliation is not specified in the biblical record, and no additional personal notes are provided. His mention highlights his role within the elite warriors serving King David.
namesAndTitles: The name Azmaveth is a proper name meaning "strong one of death" and also associated with "camel fodder" or a "plant of the plumose family." These meanings reflect Hebrew linguistic roots but the name was not specifically given by God. This reveals a name with connotations of strength and endurance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Azmaveth beyond what is listed in his unique attribute. There are no documented relatives or descendants connected to him in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Azmaveth's significance lies in his inclusion among "the thirty," the elite warriors who supported King David, marking him as a man of valor and loyalty. Being called the Barhumite identifies his origin or clan, distinguishing him within David's military ranks. His mention in the biblical narrative underscores the importance of faithful service to God's anointed king in the Old Testament.
